title: Returns: IRR, MOIC, and the drivers
objectives: Answer out loud: What are the three drivers of returns?
Answer out loud: How does holding period affect IRR?

steps.body: Three drivers of LBO returns: **EBITDA growth**, **multiple expansion**, and **debt paydown** (deleveraging).
Returns attribution splits the equity gain among these.

blocks.title: How can a PE firm increase returns?
blocks.teaser: Pay a lower purchase price, use more leverage (within reason), grow EBITDA faster (revenue growth, margin improvement), exit at a higher multiple, ex…
blocks.body:
Pay a lower purchase price, use more leverage (within reason), grow EBITDA faster (revenue growth, margin improvement), exit at a higher multiple, exit sooner, or pay dividend recaps.

**Interview answer:** "Buy cheaper, use more debt, grow EBITDA, sell at a higher multiple, or exit sooner."

blocks.title: Why do sponsors assume exit multiple = entry multiple?
blocks.teaser: Multiple expansion depends on markets, which sponsors don't control.
blocks.body: Multiple expansion depends on markets, which sponsors don't control. Assuming flat multiples tests whether the deal works on operational improvement and deleveraging alone. Underwriting multiple expansion is considered aggressive.

blocks.prompt: Why do sponsors usually underwrite exit multiple = entry multiple?

options.text: Multiple expansion depends on markets they don't control — the deal should work without it

blocks.explanation: Assuming flat multiples tests whether the deal works on operational improvement and deleveraging alone. Underwriting expansion is considered aggressive.

blocks.title: Which return driver is the "highest quality"?
blocks.teaser: EBITDA growth from operational improvement — it's repeatable and within the sponsor's control.
blocks.body: EBITDA growth from operational improvement — it's repeatable and within the sponsor's control. Multiple expansion is market-dependent; deleveraging is mechanical.

blocks.title: Why does IRR fall the longer you hold?
blocks.body: IRR is annualized. Turning $100 into $200 in 3 years ≈ 26%; in 5 years ≈ 15%. Unless value keeps compounding fast, holding longer dilutes IRR. This is why sponsors often exit around year 3–5.
